configuration: ./Config.pl -default ; ./Config.pl -u=Default -e=Mhd -ng=2 -g=10,1,1 ; ./Config.pl -opt=<the deck of ic/nominal>; deck PARAM.in from ic/<initial condition>/, run with mpiexec -n 2 and post-processed with PostProc.pl; graded: final_1d.out, log.log
observable: the final state of the 1-D linear fast wave with the Athena parameters at t = 0.5, plus the volume-average history
default_vs_upstream: upstream ships no reference for this test (its Makefile.test target has no _check step), so the pinned build generates the check's reference. Config.pl -opt is pointed at ic/nominal/PARAM.in for both initial conditions.
variant: StateVar Rho of the deck's #UNIFORMSTATE block changed from 1.0 to 1.0000000002. The change is a relative 2e-10, two units of the last digit the graded ASCII plot files print (eleven significant digits), because at four ulps of binary64 the perturbation is erased by the output format of this check and the two runs come out byte-identical. The physics is unchanged; only the round-off path of the whole run differs, so the two decks differ byte-wise, the graded files differ, and their distance is the measured floor of this pass policy.
altbuild: the same Config.pl configuration built with ./Config.pl -O0 before make BATSRUS, which sets every OPTn level of Makefile.conf to -O0 where the shipped gfortran template uses -O3; same pinned source, same deck; measured floor and margin recorded below once the selfcheck run completes

evidence.floor_how: no separate two-build floor was measured for this task: `floor` is null and the evidence for the bound is `self_validation_spread`, the nominal-versus-variant distance over every graded value of every graded file, measured by `sab.py task selfcheck` inside the declared container (Debian bookworm image, gfortran 12, Open MPI 4.1, 8 cpus, 2 MPI ranks) on the x86 worker. Where upstream ships a reference for this deck, the Step 1 native investigation reproduced it within upstream's own DiffNum tolerance on a different compiler and MPI stack (gfortran 15.2 with Open MPI 5 on macOS/arm64) from the one the reference was blessed on; that cross-platform agreement is quoted in the warrant and is the second piece of evidence. A dedicated two-build or two-toolchain floor would sharpen both and is left as an open item for the reviewer.

warrant: The graded observable is the final state of the 1-D linear fast wave with the Athena parameters at t = 0.5, plus the volume-average history, compared value by value under an absolute bound of 1e-7 with no relative term. Physical: the linear fast magnetosonic wave of Stone et al. (2008), the standard convergence problem of the Athena test suite, with their state (rho = 1, B = (1, sqrt(2), 0.5), p = 0.6) on 10-cell blocks; the wave is a smooth eigenmode, so the graded profile measures the amplitude and phase error of the scheme rather than its shock capturing. Upstream ships no reference output for this deck, so the reference is generated by the pinned build itself and the physics of the example anchors the check. A wrong port is rejected by a wide margin: a wrong eigenvalue, a dissipation coefficient that is too large or a reconstruction that is one order too low damps the eigenmode measurably over the half time unit; because the mode is smooth there is no limiter clipping to hide behind. Achievable: the run uses a fixed time step on a smooth eigenmode, so neither the CFL feedback nor a limiter branch is active over most of the domain: a four-ulp perturbation of the initial density is erased by the eleven significant digits the ASCII plot prints and the two runs come out byte-identical. The variant of this check is therefore two units of the last printed digit (2e-10 relative), and the measured spread of 2.0e-10 is that perturbation carried through undamped, which is what a non-amplifying scheme should do. The bound is a hundred times the resolution of the graded output rather than a chaos measurement.
